LESSON: READING SYLLABLES

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2
Subject: General
Strand: READING
Topic 2.3: Reading Syllables
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading Syllables, part of READING in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2 General.

Key inquiry question: Where can we read letter sounds from?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. Identify syllables from a variety of texts,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading Syllables in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. read syllables by joining 2 letter sounds; fa-fu ha-hu,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading Syllables in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. chant rhymes related to syllables,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading Syllables in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. enjoy chanting rhymes related to syllable reading. ● Listen to recorded syllables from a digital device. ● Identify written letter sounds. ● Join two sound to form syllables. ● Read the syllables fa fe fi fo fu ga ge gi go gu ha he hi ho hu on flash cards, books, charts, writing board, digital device. Learners with speech difficulties could read an audiobook or use audio visuals with subtitles to read syllables ● Chant rhymes on letter sounds collaboratively and as individuals. Learners with speech difficulties could identify the rhymes of the letters of alphabet as others chant ● Play games related to letter sounds and syllables using flash cards. Learner with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional part of the body to play. Where can we read letter sounds from?

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading Syllables in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading Syllables together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
• Respect: The learner takes turns with others to chant letters of the alphabet and read syllables.

• Unity: The learner works collaboratively with others as a team in chanting letter sounds.

● Love: The learner appreciates the effort of others by clapping.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

2. read syllables by joining 2 letter sounds; fa-fu ha-hu,
3. chant rhymes related to syllables,
